name: Karioitahi Beach
access: Karioitahi Rd off Waiuku-Karioitahi Rd, ~1 h 20 from CBD. Car park at the surf club.
best: Black sand surf beach backed by 60 m cliffs and dunes - the most dramatic flying in Auckland, north or south.
hazards: Active paraglider and hang-glider site (give way and stay well clear), strong onshore wind, surf and rips, soft sand kills motors.
note: Airspace is completely clean - 24 km from the nearest aerodrome. This is the best single spot in South Auckland by a distance. Pin is the main beach access off Karioitahi Road; the sand runs about 5 km south from here.

name: Orere Point
land: Council reserve / beach + regional park nearby
access: Orere Point Rd off Kawakawa-Orere Rd, ~1 h 05 from CBD. Beach reserve at the end.
best: Rocky coast, pohutukawa, bush and the Hauraki Gulf - cliffs and reefs give you lines you don't get on a flat beach.
hazards: Rocks and tide, boat ramp traffic, shorebirds, the regional park north of the point needs a permit.
note: Clean airspace. The reserve is local council land; the bush north is regional park, so keep to the coast strip.

name: Waiau Pa
access: Waiau Pa Rd to the wharf, ~50 min from CBD.
best: Quiet Manukau Harbour settlement with a wharf, tidal flats and shell banks - flat water and big skies.
hazards: Mudflats at low tide, shorebirds on the shell banks, wharf fishermen.
note: No permit. One of the quietest accessible spots in the south.

name: Clarks Beach
access: Clarks Beach Rd, ~50 min from CBD. Beach reserve and boat ramp.
best: Harbour beach with a long tidal flat, boats and the Awhitu hills across the water.
hazards: Boat ramp traffic in summer, mudflats, shorebirds.
note: No permit. Good at high tide; at low tide you're flying over mud.

name: Clevedon
access: Clevedon village, ~40 min from CBD. Domain and river reserve.
best: Rolling farmland, the Wairoa river, bush remnants and the Hunua foothills - rural lines with real depth.
hazards: Private farmland everywhere (don't cross it), stock, river users, and Ardmore's 4 km ring is 7 km away so you're clear.
note: No permit for the village reserves. For farmland you need the owner's permission - Part 101 requires it anyway.

name: Waiuku
access: Waiuku town, ~55 min from CBD. Estuary reserve at the wharf.
best: Estuary, moored boats, the old steel mill skyline and harbour flats - industrial-meets-coastal.
hazards: Town traffic, boats, mudflats, shorebirds.
note: No permit. Most useful as the staging town for Karioitahi 10 minutes away.

name: Glenbrook Beach
access: Glenbrook Beach Rd, ~55 min from CBD.
best: Small quiet beach on the harbour with bush and farmland behind - you'll often be alone.
hazards: Narrow road, mudflats, no facilities, NZ Steel works nearby (industrial backdrop).
note: No permit, clean airspace. Combine with Clarks Beach and Waiuku in one run.

name: Matakawau Point
access: Awhitu Rd to Matakawau Point, ~1 h 30 from CBD.
best: Tiny harbour settlement with a wharf and tidal creek - the quietest water in the south.
hazards: Mudflats, one-lane road, no phone coverage in patches.
note: No permit. Pairs with Awhitu Regional Park if you're doing the peninsula.

name: Karaka
access: Karaka, ~35 min from CBD. Karaka Sports Park or the waterfront reserve.
best: Lifestyle blocks, horse country and open sky - room for long-range runs with few people.
hazards: Inside the Auckland Model Aero Club danger area (NZ D225) - legal to fly, but watch for model traffic. Private land elsewhere.
note: Danger areas are legal but shared. Stay on council land and keep your eyes up.

name: Bombay
access: Bombay off SH1, ~40 min from CBD. Domain and hall reserve.
best: Rolling hill country, shelter belts and big views back to the Manukau - genuinely empty.
hazards: State highway traffic, private farmland, stock.
note: No permit on the domain. Everything around it is private - stay on the reserve or get permission.

name: Kingseat
access: Kingseat Rd, ~50 min from CBD.
best: Former psychiatric hospital grounds turned village - mature trees, old buildings and open fields.
hazards: Private land around the village, derelict buildings are not public access, stock.
note: Clean airspace and quiet, but the interesting buildings are mostly private. Treat it as a rural open-space fly.

name: Pukekohe
access: Pukekohe, ~45 min from CBD. Domain or the showgrounds.
best: Town parks, the racecourse and market gardens - utility flying rather than scenery.
hazards: 6.5 km from Pukekohe aerodrome so you're outside the 4 km ring, but light aircraft are active in the area.
note: Only worth it if you're local. Franklin's coast is a much better use of the drive.

name: Ararimu
access: Ararimu Rd, off Paparimu Rd; park on the verge and don't block gates.
best: Rolling farmland and shelterbelts with long open lines in every direction.
hazards: Private land, stock, farm machinery, narrow roads.
note: Ask the landowner before launching — the whole valley is private farmland.

name: Pollok
access: Pollok Rd, off Awhitu Rd; verge parking only.
best: Hill country above the Manukau with big views and no people.
hazards: Private farmland, stock, gravel roads, wind.
note: Permission needed — this is working farmland, not reserve.

name: Ramarama
access: Ramarama Rd, off State Highway 1; park at the hall.
best: Market gardens and open flats with the Bombay hills behind.
hazards: Greenhouses and polythene, orchard netting, highway traffic, private land.
note: Greenhouse country — watch for netting and stay off the crops.

name: Paerata
access: Paerata Rd, off Great South Rd.
best: Open farmland with the Drury hills and the harbour beyond.
hazards: Earthworks and new subdivisions, highway, private land.
note: Changing fast with the Drury development — check the ground before you go.

name: Mauku
access: Mauku Rd, off Glenbrook Rd; park at the hall.
best: Quiet dairy country with drains, hedgerows and long flat lines.
hazards: Stock, drains, private land, milk tankers on the road.
note: Ask first — the paddocks are all in production.

name: Kohekohe
access: Kohekohe Rd, off Awhitu Rd; verge parking.
best: Deep rural Awhitu — hills, bush remnants and nobody for kilometres.
hazards: Private land, stock, gravel, no phone coverage.
note: The most remote spot on the Awhitu road; permission essential.

name: Patumahoe
access: Patumahoe Rd; park at the domain.
best: Village domain and surrounding farmland — easy access, open skies.
hazards: Village traffic, private paddocks, sport on the domain.
note: Launch from the domain and fly the edges; ask before crossing into paddocks.

name: Puni
access: Puni Rd, off Great South Rd.
best: Flat farmland on the Puni flats — open airspace and nothing to hit.
hazards: Private land, stock, State Highway 1 nearby.
note: Simple open-country flying; permission needed.
